hero.title: Miftahuddin Islamic Institute
hero.headline: A Key to Faith, Knowledge and Service
hero.subtitle: Rooted in Kimberley, Miftahuddin carries the light of Islamic education, compassionate welfare and heartfelt da'wah across the Northern Cape, the Free State and beyond.

intro.title: An Institute Built on Three Pillars
intro.body: Miftahuddin Islamic Institute is a Kimberley-based Islamic organisation whose name — meaning "Key of the Deen" — reflects its mission: to unlock knowledge, compassion and faith for the communities it serves. Through a growing network of Makaatib, Masaajid and welfare programmes reaching across the Northern Cape and into the Free State, Miftahuddin exists to preserve Islamic identity, uplift the vulnerable and strengthen the bonds of community.

items.title: Ta'leem
items.subtitle: Education
items.body: A network of Makaatib safeguards the Islamic identity of children from their earliest years, connecting them to the Deen through structured Qur'anic and Islamic education.

items.title: Social Welfare
items.subtitle: Khidmah
items.body: From feeding schemes to bursaries and prison outreach, Miftahuddin's welfare work is an expression of Imaan — rooted in the Sunnah of the Prophet ﷺ, who showed us compassion and justice for those in need.

items.title: Tableegh
items.subtitle: Outreach
items.body: Miftahuddin strengthens Ukhuwwah within the community by means of Dawah and Tableegh, showing the qualities of Islam to others — Tableegh and Jamaat to Muslims, Dawah to non-Muslims — striving always to strengthen our Ukhuwwah and our Imaan and obedience to Allah Ta'ala.

hero.title: Our Story
hero.subtitle: A Kimberley-based Islamic institute carrying Ta'leem, Social Welfare and Tableegh to communities across the Northern Cape and Free State.

history.title: Since 1974
paragraphs: Alhamdulillah, through the grace of Allah Ta'ala, Miftahuddin Islamic Institute has been in existence for over fifty years, since its inception in 1974. The Institute was established primarily for the assistance of poor and underprivileged people who ascribe to the Islamic faith, and secondarily for the needs of other underprivileged people wherever possible.

Assistance has been extended in many forms over the decades — distributing food parcels and clothing, slaughtering and distributing meat, running feeding schemes, facilitating religious education, offering moral guidance and counselling, arranging funerals, educating prisoners, seeing to the expenses of religious ceremonies such as marriages, distributing money, food and clothing for the Eid festivals, and maintaining the Darul 'Ajaaib Islamic Museum as a source of Da'wah to visitors.

Each year, the Mini-Mina Qurbani Camp sees approximately 400 sheep, goats and cows slaughtered, with the meat distributed to Muslims and non-Muslims alike, while Ramadhaan brings Iftaar and Sehri to Miftahuddin's centres — and to the inmates of the prisons it serves.

legacy.title: Ulama Raised, Communities Served
legacy.body: Over the decades, close to forty Huffadh and thirty Ulama have qualified through Miftahuddin's efforts, alongside many Daa'ees, Aalimahs, Apas and Haafidhas. Alhamdulillah, they remain engaged in Deeni Khidmah — teaching in Madaaris or leading Salaah in Masaajid across the network.

editorial.title: Why Our Work Matters
paragraphs: In today's world, where the gap between the rich and poor continues to grow, social welfare work is more important than ever. Miftahuddin Islamic Institute, built on values of compassion, justice and community support, is dedicated to fighting poverty and helping those in need.

Social welfare is all about helping people who are struggling to meet their basic needs — food, clothing, education and shelter. For us, these actions are more than charity; they are part of our Imaan and our commitment to Islamic teaching. Zakat, one of the Five Pillars of Islam, requires Muslims to give a portion of their wealth to those less fortunate — not only to purify wealth, but to ensure the community thrives.

Poverty affects millions worldwide, leading to a lack of essentials like food, shelter and education. Our goal is to break this cycle by providing financial help and education to those in need, empowering people to improve their lives and contribute to society.

items.title: Ta'leem — Education
items.body: The Makaatib system is the backbone of our educational efforts. Besides empowering children through education, it serves as their primary connection to the Deen of Islam — essential to the preservation of their Imaan and Islamic identity. As the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) said, "Seeking knowledge is an obligation upon every Muslim."

items.title: Social Welfare — Khidmah
items.body: Our welfare work strengthens community bonds by bringing people together through feeding schemes, bursaries, hostels and assistance to the poor, orphans and travellers. The Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) said, "The best of people are those who are most beneficial to others."

items.title: Tableegh — Outreach & Ukhuwwah
items.body: By encouraging mutual support and collective action, Miftahuddin fosters Ukhuwwah in line with the Qur'an: "The believers are but brothers, so make settlement between your brothers. And fear Allah that you may receive mercy." (49:10)

quote.arabic: من لم يشكر الناس لم يشكر الله
quote.translation: "He who is not thankful to man cannot be thankful to Allah Ta'ala."

thankYouDonors.body: "We cannot be grateful enough to all those who gave moral, physical, monetary and any other form of support to the institution for the sake of Allah. We continually make du'a that Allah Ta'ala reward them abundantly in Dunya and Aakhirah with all goodness and well-being."

values.title: Our Educational Philosophy
values.body: Miftahuddin holds that seeking knowledge is an obligation upon every Muslim, and that the preservation of Islamic identity begins in childhood. Through the Makaatib system, feeding schemes and community welfare, education and compassion are treated as inseparable — each strengthening the other in service of a fair and God-conscious society.

hero.title: Ta'leem: Our Educational Role
hero.subtitle: Structured Islamic education that safeguards Imaan and identity, from early childhood through to advanced Islamic scholarship.

intro.title: The Makaatib System
paragraphs: At the heart of Miftahuddin's educational mission is the Makaatib system — a network of Islamic schools that instils Qur'anic literacy and Islamic character in children from their earliest years. Besides empowering children through education, the Makaatib serve as their primary connection to the Deen of Islam, essential to the preservation of their Imaan and Islamic identity.

This network extends well beyond Kimberley, reaching small towns across the vast Northern Cape and into the Free State — including dedicated provision for a Hifz class, a girls' Madrasah with boarding, and Madrasah classes held within correctional facilities. There are four such facilities in the Northern Cape — two in Kimberley, one in Douglas and one in Upington — as well as two in the Free State.

Seeking knowledge is highly valued in Islam. The Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) said, "Seeking knowledge is an obligation upon every Muslim." Promoting education in this spirit helps fulfil that duty and empowers our community.

socialWelfare.title: Makaatib and Social Welfare
paragraphs: Since our Makaatib are in predominantly disadvantaged areas, the majority of the students arrive hungry at Madressah. Their first meal was probably at the beginning of the day before going to school. Some go hungry and only eat again at night. There is therefore a need to give them some sort of provision to continue for the day.

Thus, Alhamdulillah, all the Makaatib in Kimberley — and one of the Maktabs outside of Kimberley — have snacks provided every day to the students, and a hot, freshly prepared meal is given to them on Fridays. Occasionally, this is extended to the other Makaatib outside of Kimberley as well, as and when we are able to.

reach.title: A Network Across Two Provinces
reach.body: Alhamdulillah, effort in the vast Northern Cape is ongoing. The Northern Cape alone makes up approximately 30% of the total area of South Africa, meaning travel between our Makaatib and Masaajid is fairly challenging — yet much progress continues to be made each year.

beyondMakaatib.title: Beyond the Makaatib
beyondMakaatib.body: Miftahuddin also sponsors students studying in various local Madrasahs — assisting with travel, clothing and meals — as well as students pursuing advanced Islamic scholarship in Darul Ulooms and other institutes of learning. Aid has also been extended to underprivileged students pursuing a secular course of their choice, and feeding schemes ensure that no child attending our Maktab goes hungry.

future.title: Madrassah Tamim ul Banaat
future.body: Madrassah Tamim ul Banaat is Miftahuddin's boarding Madressah for girls — part of the wider Makaatib network described above, giving female students structured Islamic education alongside safe, residential accommodation for the duration of their Deeni studies.

qurbani.title: Reviving the Spirit of Qurbani
paragraphs: A need was seen many years ago that the spirit of Qurbani has to be revived in Kimberley and the Northern Cape, and Alhamdulillah Maulana M.E. Jeena, after consultation with his elders, decided to have a Qurbani camp in Kimberley, where people will be encouraged to slaughter the animals as well as fulfil the Sunnah as a solution to those who are in need.
Keeping that in mind, it was started. Currently it takes place in two areas in Kimberley — Roodepan and Colville.

On the first day, approximately 250 sheep are slaughtered, and another 150 or so over the next two days. Distribution takes place of a greater portion of the meat in the days of Qurbani, with food being cooked and fed to those who are present, and meat parcels distributed to those who are present.
Besides that, every other part of the animal is also distributed — the kop (head), the pootjies (feet), and so on.

It also serves as a form of Dawah to the non-Muslims, where Hadhrat Maulana M.E. Jeena himself, whether it is hot or cold, will stand on the Mimbar and give Dawah to all the non-Muslims who are waiting for a small parcel at the end of the day.

Alhamdulillah, it has become a way and means for many people entering into Islam, and many people's perception of Islam has also changed due to them seeing the generosity of the Muslims and the Ukhuwwah of the Muslims.

network.title: Kimberley, the Northern Cape & the Free State
network.body: Miftahuddin's Makaatib, Masaajid and Musallahs span Kimberley's townships and reach into small towns including Windsorton, Prieska, Kathu, Douglas, Griekwastad, Hopetown, Britstown, Victoria West, Olifantshoek and Upington in the Northern Cape, and Koffiefontein, Jagersfontein, Boshof and Dealesville in the Free State.
network.growth: Earlier reports identified new Masaajid in Dealesville and Boshof as urgent, unmet needs. Alhamdulillah, both have since been completed — a small but telling sign of Miftahuddin's steady expansion despite the vast distances involved.

items.title: A New Masjid for Kimberley's CBD
items.summary: A church was bought, Alhamdulillah, with the help of generous donors, and Salaah has started with a dedicated Imam — though the Masjid is not yet open to the public.
items.body: A historic church in the heart of Kimberley's CBD has been transformed into a Masjid, Alhamdulillah, with the help of generous donors. Its soaring wooden-beamed roof and stained-glass windows now frame a new mihrab, set beneath geometric Islamic pattern-work and calligraphy. Salaah has started with a dedicated Imam, but the Masjid is not yet complete or open to the public — we are still waiting for the arrival of Musallahs and finishing the remaining work. It will serve the broader CBD area and the wider community of Kimberley once ready.
marquee: A former church, reborn as a house of Allah
Not yet open to the public — renovations continuing
Musallahs are still needed to finish the Masjid

items.title: Renovations Under Way at the CBD Masjid
items.summary: Our team is on-site right now finishing the grounds and facilities so the Masjid can be fully completed.
items.body: Work continues on-site at the new CBD Masjid, Alhamdulillah. Contractors and volunteers are pressing ahead with the final stages of the conversion — finishing the grounds, sorting out ablution facilities, and preparing for the Musallahs still to arrive. The photo below captures the Masjid mid-transformation, a reminder that every stage of this project has been carried by the generosity of donors.
